subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TS module for a static six-wheeled vehicle model built with createBuilder, using boxes and cylinders to form a cab, chassis, wheels, and a railgun mounted on top, sized to stand properly at ground level.

I'm sketching out helper functions for boxes and cylinders, confirming no joints are needed since the model is static, and choosing a color palette of olive armor, steel, orange accents, and cyan glow details. Now I'm working out the wheel and chassis dimensions, spacing three wheels per side along the hull and positioning the tire radius and axle placement.

Each wheel gets a tire, rim, hub, and small lug bolts, with fenders boxed over them, and I'm checking the hull proportions so the wheels overlap the hull sides correctly. Then I'm shaping the cab at the front with a sloped windshield using a rotated box, glowing dark-cyan windows, and planning a railgun mounted on top toward the rear.

Now I'm laying out the railgun: twin parallel rail boxes running most of the hull length, a barrel shroud cylinder, a rear breech block, capacitor bank cylinders with orange bands along the sides, glowing coil rings spaced along the rails, dark insulator blocks between the rails, A-frame support pylons, and muzzle brackets. I'm noticing the cab roof might clip the barrel height, so I'm raising the barrel's y-position to clear the cab.

Now I'm adjusting the cradle pylons so they span the deck up to the raised barrel height on either side of the cab, letting the barrel pass over the cab roof with clearance, and adding stabilizer outriggers positioned between the wheel locations to brace the hull.

I'm sketching the leg geometry: a horizontal arm from the hull out to a vertical hydraulic cylinder, ending in a flat foot pad, plus a diagonal brace rod tying the arm back to the hull for rigidity, making sure the leg placement along the hull doesn't collide with the wheel positions.

Four legs confirmed with both sides mirrored. Now I'm planning the detail pass: headlights, hazard stripe pads, armor panels with bolts, emblem box, antenna, radar dish, smoke launchers, exhausts, tanks, hatches, ladder, tow hooks, mirrors, side skirts, and rear lights, aiming for roughly 200 parts total with wheels and pads sitting flush at ground level. I'm starting to write a helper function for creating boxes with position and options.

Writing cylinder helpers...

Placing lug bolts as small cylinders arranged radially at the set radius, then setting rotation values in XYZ degrees for each part before writing out the full wheel assembly code.
